heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini handles Sunlu PETG effortlessly out of the box with its stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame architecture. By capping the maximum volumetric flow rate to 15 mm³/s, the machine safely sustains peak print speeds of up to 179 mm/s with exceptional layer bonding.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with glue stick or liquid glue applied as a release agent to prevent bed surface damage
slicerTweaks: Set 'Max volumetric speed' to 15 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent underextrusion at high feedrates.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' with a 1.5 mm wipe distance to eliminate stringing and nozzle buildup inherent to sticky PETG.
Disable part cooling for the first 3 layers, and maintain fan speeds between 20% and 50% for structural integrity.
Set Pressure Advance (PA / Flow Dynamics) to approximately 0.036 via calibration to avoid corner bulging and seam blobbing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Fine stringing and branching across open travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Sunlu PETG is highly hygroscopic and tends to ooze when saturated with atmospheric moisture, aggravated by excess nozzle heat.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 hours and reduce printing temperature from 245°C to 238°C in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing or permanent fusion to the build surface
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG creates an aggressive chemical bond with smooth PEI surfaces, causing plate damage during removal.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Print exclusively on the Bambu Textured PEI plate and apply a thin layer of PVA glue stick to serve as a sacrificial release interface.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak layer adhesion and brittle parts along the Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds exceeding 60% cause premature crystallization and rapid layer chilling.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower 'Part Cooling Fan' maximum limit to 40% in the filament cooling settings and verify nozzle temperature is at least 240°C.

faq.question: Does Sunlu PETG require an enclosure on the Bambu Lab A1 Mini?
faq.answer: No, PETG does not suffer from extreme shrinkage like ABS or ASA and prints reliably in open-air environments without draft-related delamination.

faq.question: Can the A1 Mini bed reach the required temperature for Sunlu PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, Sunlu PETG performs reliably at 70°C to 78°C, which falls cleanly within the A1 Mini hardware limit of 80°C.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for Sunlu PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard Sunlu PETG is non-abrasive, making the stock stainless steel nozzle completely suitable and wear-resistant for this material.

faq.question: Why is glue stick required on the Textured PEI plate for PETG?
faq.answer: PETG adheres aggressively to PEI coatings; the glue stick acts as a release barrier rather than an adhesive, preventing the filament from ripping chunks out of the plate surface.
